sections.title: Years and the past of van
sections.content: You know *-ban/-ben* from A1, and a year takes it too: *1848-ban* means "in 1848". When you write the digits, a hyphen joins the ending to the number. You know the past of *van*, *volt* (Unit 24), so one short sentence tells what the holiday remembers: *1848-ban forradalom volt Magyarországon.* You also know *szabadnap* (Unit 1): the national holidays are days off. Saint Stephen is remembered as the first Hungarian king, *király*: *Szent István az első magyar király volt.* (*első* is from Unit 2.)

items.english: In 1848 there was a revolution in Hungary.
In 1956 too there was a revolution in Budapest.

items.spanish: Szent István az első magyar király volt.
items.english: Saint Stephen was the first Hungarian king.
On 23 October it is a day off.

sections.content: Use *volt* for something in the past and *van* for now: *1956-ban forradalom volt*, *ma szabadnap van*. With a plural subject use *voltak*.
